answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the ember check immediately, the garden audit keeps the resolved set and the dawn replay shows exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 263 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 263 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
